package_info.package_manager: source (system/library package, not typical package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: These versions contain buffer overflow vulnerabilities (CVE-2022-3602 and CVE-2022-3786) in the X.509 certificate email address punycode decoding functions. Attackers can exploit these flaws by presenting specially crafted certificates, leading to denial of service (crash) or, in rare cases, remote code execution during certificate verification.

execution_context.trigger: During certificate verification (runtime, during TLS handshake)
execution_context.file_location: X.509 certificate parsing (punycode decoding in name constraint check)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: A buffer overrun can be triggered in X.509 certificate verification. To be specific, it happens in the name constraint check. An attacker can craft a malicious email address to overflow an arbitrary number of bytes containing the . (decimal 46) character on the stack.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During certificate verification (runtime, during TLS handshake), the code decodes a maliciously crafted email address in an X.509 certificate using the punycode decoding function, allowing attacker-controlled input to overrun a stack buffer with repeated '.' (decimal 46) characters, resulting in stack corruption and process crash (denial of service).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Buffer overflows in cryptographic libraries, especially during certificate parsing of untrusted input, are highly suspicious as they can be exploited for denial of service or further attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal certificate parsing should enforce strict bounds checking to prevent writing outside allocated buffers; here, unchecked writes to the stack are possible due to improper handling of punycode decoding.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code decodes email addresses in certificates but always enforces buffer boundaries to prevent overflows.
key_indicators: Buffer overrun in punycode decoding during X.509 name constraint check
Triggered by attacker-controlled email address field in certificate
Crash or abnormal termination of OpenSSL process during certificate verification

execution_context.file_location: X.509 certificate parsing (punycode decoding in name constraint check)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: CVE-2022-3602 is an arbitrary 4-byte stack buffer overflow. Such vulnerabilities may lead to remote code execution.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During certificate verification (runtime, during TLS handshake), the code decodes a maliciously crafted email address in an X.509 certificate, causing a 4-byte stack buffer overflow on the stack, which may allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code on certain platforms.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Stack buffer overflows in security-critical code paths are a classic vector for code execution, especially when triggered by attacker-supplied certificate fields.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Certificate parsing routines must never allow writing outside stack buffer boundaries; this vulnerability allows a 4-byte overflow, violating memory safety.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate code decodes email addresses with strict bounds checking, preventing any buffer overflow.
key_indicators: 4-byte stack buffer overflow in punycode decoding
Triggered by attacker-controlled email address field in X.509 certificate
Potential for remote code execution if stack is overwritten with attacker-controlled data
Abnormal process termination or exploitation during certificate verification

attack_chain.action: Attacker obtains or forges a malicious X.509 certificate with a specially crafted email address field designed to exploit the punycode decoding vulnerability.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious certificate is presented to a vulnerable OpenSSL client or server during a TLS handshake.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable OpenSSL instance parses the certificate and decodes the email address using the punycode decoding function, processing attacker-controlled input.
attack_chain.leads_to: Buffer overflow occurs on the stack during certificate verification.

attack_chain.action: The buffer overflow results in either a process crash (denial of service) or, in rare cases, remote code execution if the stack is overwritten with attacker-controlled data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Denial of service or potential remote code execution on the vulnerable system.

behavioral_signatures: Stack buffer overflows or memory corruption detected during X.509 certificate parsing in OpenSSL processes
Crashes or abnormal termination of OpenSSL-based applications during or immediately after certificate verification
Unexpected process termination when handling certificates with unusually long or punycode-encoded email address fields
file_indicators: X.509 certificates containing unusually long or punycode-encoded email address fields
Certificates with repeated '.' (decimal 46) characters in the email address field
Certificates with email address fields exceeding typical length or containing suspicious punycode sequences
network_indicators: TLS connections where the peer presents certificates with suspiciously encoded or excessively long email address fields
Repeated failed TLS handshakes from the same source, correlated with process crashes on the server or client
Unusual spikes in certificate verification failures or process restarts in OpenSSL-based services
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor OpenSSL-based applications for crashes, abnormal terminations, or memory corruption events during TLS handshakes, especially when processing certificates with long or punycode-encoded email addresses. Use static analysis or software composition analysis (SCA) tools to identify deployments of OpenSSL versions 3.0.0-3.0.6. Inspect certificate fields for suspicious patterns, such as repeated '.' characters, excessive length, or punycode sequences in email addresses. Correlate network logs for repeated failed handshakes with process crashes to identify exploitation attempts.
